title: Joe Klessy gives him a string bass
summary: After a mix-up with composer Nick Klessy, Sherwood describes bandleader Joe Klessy, who lent him a string bass when he was playing sousaphone.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Is that the fellow composed some of those numbers?
No, no, I think you have in mind a man composed, I'm sorry I made you cry. What's his name?
N.J. Nick. Nick Klessy, I think.

Nick Klessy, I think. I think he was a realtor. I couldn't say. I don't know. But anyhow, Joe Klessy was the type of guy that would give you the shirt off his back. And he said to me one night, I was playing sousaphone then, only the sousaphone, he said, Why don't you get a string bass? Well in those days you'd play all night for three bucks, you know, and nobody could afford two or three instruments. I was paying for a bass on at the time and I told him, Well I can't afford that. And I don't know if I'd have the coordination never having tried it, you know. I said, It takes some coordination to play a string bass. So, he said, I have one. Come get it and take it home, keep it as long as you want. He was playing drums at the time. So I took the bass home and like I told you before, my grandfather came over and showed me how to tune it. And then I just went on from there with it.
